nodes.label: Node.js 24+ support
nodes.rationale: Fully supported and CI'd alongside Bun; chosen for managed platforms, LTS compliance regimes, existing Node infrastructure, and wider native-module support.

nodes.label: Node 24 as the supported floor
nodes.rationale: Node 24 is the oldest active LTS line (20 is EOL as of April 2026, 22 is maintenance) and the first floor where WebCrypto subtle, fetch, a native WebSocket client, native zstd and AsyncLocalStorage all ship natively, removing several fallbacks.

nodes.label: Node peer dependencies
nodes.rationale: Lazy imports mean a missing optional peer only breaks the feature that instantiates it, so users install per subsystem rather than up front.

nodes.label: better-sqlite3 native build requirements
nodes.rationale: It is a native module needing gyp, Python and a C++ compiler on first install; alpine images must add build tools or use the Debian-based official node image.

nodes.label: Cluster model does not fit Lambda
nodes.rationale: Actors expect a long-running process, so short-lived invocations should use a single-actor-per-invocation pattern rather than clustering; the same caveat covers Cloud Functions, Vercel and Netlify.

nodes.label: ESM-only distribution
nodes.rationale: actor-ts ships type: module; CommonJS consumers need a build step to bridge, so using ESM throughout is the easier path.

nodes.label: Node performance profile
nodes.rationale: Roughly 6-8M tells/sec and 300-500 ms startup against Bun's sub-100 ms; the startup gap is irrelevant for long-running services and only matters for tight-loop throughput work.
